messages.content: How did I sleep last night?

content.text:
Last night was a **fair** night. Your sleep score was **74/100**, and the main thing holding it back was how short it was.

**Timing:** You fell asleep around **23:11** and woke at about **05:52**. That's 6h 41m in bed, with **6h 15m of actual sleep**.

**Sleep stages:**
| Stage | Time | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Deep | 1h 10m | 18.7% |
| Light | 3h 45m | 60.0% |
| REM | 1h 20m | 21.3% |
| Awake | 26m | 1 wake-up |

**Other numbers:**
- **Overnight HRV:** 58 ms on average
- **Stress during sleep:** 14 on average, which is low and calm
- **Blood oxygen (SpO2):** 95% on average. Your lowest reading was 88%. Brief dips like this are common, and wrist sensors aren't very accurate overnight. If it keeps happening and you also snore or wake up tired, it's worth checking.

**Bottom line:** Your deep and REM sleep made up a healthy share of the night, and you woke up only once. You just didn't sleep long enough. Most adults need 7–9 hours, so going to bed 45–60 minutes earlier would probably raise your score. If you were planning a hard workout today, you might keep it a bit lighter.
